headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and cascading misuse: Mentat can write shared files while social-auto-upload can act on media/account files, creating dangerous cross-agent interference.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, so malicious content in shared files could influence it. social-auto-upload also consumes local media/account files, but no shared parser or MCP bridge is documented. The pathway exists mainly through manual or file-based handoff, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory of user-controlled files, prompt-like content can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions rather than data, injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Separate working directories for the two agents.
Rename or quarantine untrusted text files before Mentat reads them.
Require manual review of any file content passed between agents.
Disable shared clipboard or ad hoc copy-paste workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted instruction-like content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat has broad network egress and reads/writes filesystem content, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media files. If they share a workspace, source code or account artifacts can be exposed through Mentat's outbound API calls or through accidental reuse of files. The pair does not show a built-in isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace, files touched by one can be read by the other.
IF Mentat sends file contents to its model provider, shared sensitive files may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate directories and separate OS accounts.
Keep account files out of Mentat's input set.
Review outbound prompts before sending them to any model provider.
Store secrets in a vault, not in shared project files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can modify git state and write the filesystem, and its shared-state model is via filesystem. social-auto-upload does not write files, but it does operate on account files and broad network egress. The main conflict is that Mentat's default write access can race with file-based automation, causing corrupted media/account artifacts or inconsistent uploads; uncertainty about orchestration pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or media directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF social-auto-upload reads files while Mentat is rewriting them, uploads may use partial or stale content.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Put social-auto-upload outputs in a separate staging folder.
Commit or snapshot files before Mentat edits them.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes and lock coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and social-auto-upload can act on local media/account files and then push them to external platforms. If social-auto-upload consumes Mentat-generated artifacts without verification, a bad edit can cascade into incorrect or public-facing uploads. The downstream action-taking authority makes the blast radius large.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses files produced by Mentat as upload inputs, any mistaken edit can propagate externally.
IF no human review occurs between Mentat's proposal and upload execution, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require manual approval before upload.
Diff-check media and metadata against source files.
Use a dry-run mode for uploads.
Keep Mentat outputs in a review-only folder.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any external post.

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles model-provider API keys and source code, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media and sends them to external services. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and residency because both rely on third-party APIs, but the profiles do not document a specific regulated data class like PHI or EU PII. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace, third-party transmission may violate policy.
IF retention expectations differ between the model provider and the upload platform, logs may persist longer than intended.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files.
Review retention settings for both external services.
Separate account data from source-code workspaces.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
